caption_link.limitation: The source provides matching numeric IDs only. It does not provide an original post URL, date, media link, or an explicit asset-to-caption key.

inspection.evidence_scope: Source-bound start, material-intermediate, and near-complete frames were extracted from the original local GIF and visually inspected; metadata came from that same source file.

motion_sampling.method: Three source-bound frame samples extracted from the original local GIF for review; no derivative was added to the corpus.
motion_sampling.limitation: The near-end sample falls during a visibly partial reset/fade. Three sampled frames establish the observed state change, not a frame-by-frame reconstruction of timing or platform playback.

visual_anatomy.title: A broad audience-growth promise gives two selected terms rough-display lavender tags; a short subtitle states that three forms should be distinguished.
visual_anatomy.layout: A three-column comparison table occupies the page. The top row is a shared time-versus-success chart; subsequent rows compare trajectory, content form, strengths, weaknesses, follower motive, audience breadth, commercial use, price scale, and creation method.
visual_anatomy.reading_order: Headline and qualification → the three named columns → shared trajectory chart → compare each row across the same three alternatives.
visual_anatomy.typography: Large light sans title with rough-display emphasis; bold compact column names and row headers; smaller list text and short quotations in the body.
visual_anatomy.colour: Pink, aqua, and lavender establish three persistent column identities over a mostly white grid with black rules.
visual_anatomy.surface: Flat editorial table with thin black cells, a lightly shaded graph area, restrained tinted rows, and no decorative illustration.
visual_anatomy.modules: One three-way comparison system: shared chart, nine labelled row bands, and one animated audience-persona row.
visual_anatomy.density: High and relational: it expects side-by-side scanning, but recurring row alignment lets the reader make comparisons without hunting.

motion.observed_state_change: The opening sample shows the stable comparison grid without the final chart curves or audience-breadth bands. In the material intermediate state, three different trajectory shapes and coloured audience bands have drawn into their shared rows; the near-end sample is visibly fading/resetting instead of introducing another semantic category.
motion.motion_job: Make temporal differences and audience-scope differences more noticeable while leaving the comparison matrix readable as a static reference.
motion.limitation: Three sampled frames establish the observed state change, not a frame-by-frame reconstruction of timing or platform playback.

transferable_mechanism.reader_job: Choose among alternatives by comparing the same decision dimensions instead of memorising disconnected descriptions.
transferable_mechanism.argument_shape: Three-way comparison matrix with one shared visual variable and repeated verbal criteria.
transferable_mechanism.mechanism: Hold each option in a fixed column, use aligned rows for the evaluation criteria, and reserve a small graph or band only for the dimension that benefits from seeing shape over time or scale.
transferable_mechanism.use_condition: Use when the alternatives genuinely share a common set of decision criteria; any rates, causal claims, or commercial implications must be supported separately.

anti_copy_boundary: Do not reuse the audience-growth subject, three named content categories, exact table rows, trajectory shapes, coloured audience bands, price markers, wording, rough-display tags, or pastel column assignment.

claim_boundary.note: The visual itself makes typological, behavioural, and commercial assertions about content. The workbook caption is only numerically associated, and the asset’s claims are not independently verified.
